article_content: The House at Hanging Rock, designed by Kerstin Thompson, draws inspiration from the site's eerie backdrop made famous by Peter Weir's 'Picnic At Hanging Rock'. Located in the Macedon Ranges, it's divided into three parallel terraces with sweeping bushland views. The design won the top award at the 2014 Australian Institute of Architecture awards. Thompson stated that 'Hanging Rock' reminds her of Weir's film, and she aimed to capture a similar enigma in her design. The house features raw insulated precast concrete walls and narrow timber shutters, blending into the landscape. It's designed for a high Bushfire Attack Level rating, ensuring safety and durability.
translated_content: Huset ved Hanging Rock, designet af Kerstin Thompson, henter inspiration fra den uhyggelige kulisse, der blev gjort berømt af Peter Weirs film 'Picnic At Hanging Rock'. Det er placeret i Macedon Ranges og er opdelt i tre parallelle terrasser med imponerende udsigt over den omkringliggende australske bush. Designet vandt toppræmien ved den australske arkitekturpris i 2014. Thompson udtalte, at navnet 'Hanging Rock' minder hende om Weirs film, og hun har forsøgt at fange en lignende mystik i sit design. Huset er karakteriseret ved rå, isolerede betonvægge og smalle træskodder, der smelter sammen med landskabet. Det er designet til at kunne modstå en høj risiko for bushbrande, hvilket sikrer både sikkerhed og holdbarhed.

article_content: Eliaquim Mangala has revealed he'd prefer a move to Chelsea rather than Manchester City because the Blues are based in London. Mangala is keen to join the club that will give him the best chance of winning silverware. 'Every player wants to play for the biggest clubs. Despite its ambitions, BRICS faces significant challenges, including a lack of cohesion and divergent economic policies.

article_content: Living at the 'China-North Korea' border, I trained under two North Korean tae kwon do masters. While I said I was learning the rare North Korean martial art, I was secretly helping North Korean refugees escape on the 6,000-mile underground railroad to 'South Korea'. In 2004, I traveled to North Korea despite many warnings. A detained Chinese worker later said North Korea had a file on me. I lived in fear of detention for years. Three American citizens, 'Kenneth Bae', 'Matthew Todd Miller', and 'Jeffrey Edward Fowle', were interviewed by CNN in Pyongyang. This was an apparent move by North Korea to attract a high-ranking U.S. official. North Korea wants control and respect, but this strategy is flawed. The regime uses these incidents to gain favor with its people. The interviews were clearly coordinated to request a high-level U.S. envoy. North Korean refugees told us of the regime's brutality, confirmed by the U.N.'s report on human rights violations. Bae, Miller, and Fowle said they were treated humanely. North Korea is walking a fine line between using them as bait and not angering the U.S. The regime has used detainees as propaganda before, but it's 'preaching to a disappearing choir' as North Koreans access more outside information.

I 2004 rejste jeg til Nordkorea trods mange advarsler. En fængslet kinesisk arbejder sagde senere, at Nordkorea havde en fil om mig. Jeg levede i frygt for fængsling i årevis. Tre amerikanske statsborgere, 'Kenneth Bae', 'Matthew Todd Miller' og 'Jeffrey Edward Fowle', blev interviewet af CNN i Pyongyang. Dette var et åbenlyst træk fra Nordkoreas side for at tiltrække en højtstående amerikansk embedsmand. Nordkorea ønsker kontrol og respekt, men strategien er mangelfuld. Regimet bruger disse hændelser til at vinde gunst hos sit folk. Interviewene var koordineret for at anmode om en højtstående amerikansk udsending. Nordkoreanske flygtninge fortalte os om regimets brutalitet, bekræftet af FN's rapport om menneskerettighedskrænkelser. Bae, Miller og Fowle sagde, de blev behandlet humant. Nordkorea går en fin linje mellem at bruge dem som lokkemad og ikke gøre USA vred. Regimet har brugt fanger som propaganda før, men det er at 'prædike for en forsvindende menighed', da nordkoreanerne i stigende grad får adgang til information udefra.

article_content: Mississippi has finally abolished slavery 148 years after the 13th Amendment was first passed by the Senate, thanks to the efforts of individuals connected to the University of Mississippi. Dr. Ranjan Batra, an associate professor at the University of Mississippi Medical Center, watched Steven Spielberg's 'Lincoln' and became curious about the state-by-state ratification process of the 13th Amendment. He found that Mississippi had not officially ratified it. The US Constitution website noted that Mississippi ratified the amendment in 1995 but failed to notify the US Archivist. Dr. Batra shared his discovery with Ken Sullivan, who recalled the 1995 vote. Sullivan obtained the necessary paperwork from the National Archives and contacted Secretary of State Delbert Hosemann, who filed the paperwork on January 30. The director of the Federal Register confirmed Mississippi's ratification on February 7.

Han opdagede, at Mississippi ikke havde ratificeret det officielt. En note på USAs forfatningswebsite anførte, at Mississippi havde ratificeret tillægget i 1995, men ikke havde underrettet USAs arkivar. Dr. Batra delte sin opdagelse med Ken Sullivan, som huskede afstemningen i 1995. Sullivan fik den nødvendige dokumentation fra National Archives og kontaktede Secretary of State Delbert Hosemann, som indsendte papirerne den 30. januar. Direktøren for Federal Register bekræftede Mississippis ratifikation den 7. februar.'

article_content: (CNN) -- As the eye of the storm approaches, most people head home, but for surfers eager to ride the waves of the winter storms, it's a different story. Europe may have escaped the icy grip of the 'Polar Vortex' that has ravaged the U.S., but storms on the continent have brought widespread flooding and disruption in the new year. For hardcore surfers, this is a time of abundance, not scarcity; they're having a great time. The low-pressure systems sweeping in from the Atlantic have drawn surfers to chase the so-called 'Black Swell,' with world-class athletes traveling to the west coast of France to ride the waves forming off the famous Belharra reef in Basque Country. American surfer Shane Dorian flew from Hawaii to join some of Europe's top surfers, including Justine Dupont and Benjamin Sanchis, for a once-in-a-lifetime chance to ride the big Belharra swell. 'Belharra, take me to your arms,' Sanchis wrote on his Facebook page, while Dorian said: 'Paddled into a few at #Belharra today in the south of France.' Although the waters peaked during the night, Dorian and his fellow surfers still enjoyed a surf session at a spot where surfers are usually towed out to the massive waves by jet skis. French 1998 World Cup winner Bixente Lizarazu, an avid surfer since retiring from football, also surfed at Belharra. On Ireland's west coast, stormy weather and massive waves attracted surfers to the popular spot Mullaghmore Head. The U.K. has prepared for high winds and heavy rain, but even in the smaller waves along the British coast, intrepid surfers ignored the Met Office's safety advice to brave the waters. It seems that when the surf's up, the hardcore surfers are out riding the waves.

Amerikaneren Shane Dorian fløj fra Hawaii for at mødes med nogle af Europas bedste surfere, herunder Justine Dupont og Benjamin Sanchis, for en chance for at ride den store Belharra dønning. 'Belharra, tag mig til dig,' skrev Sanchis på Facebook, mens Dorian sagde: 'Paddlet ud til et par bølger ved #Belharra i dag i det sydlige Frankrig.' article_content: Digital currencies like Bitcoin are increasingly being used by divorcing spouses to hide wealth from their partners during court battles. Ayesha Vardag, a London divorce lawyer, has claimed that forums devoted to Bitcoin have been filled with husbands discussing the option of using digital currencies. It is feared that spouses could use Bitcoin to hide wealth by transferring the currency between online wallets, to friends, or to areas outside of legal jurisdiction. Ayesha Vardag said that more divorce lawyers could start including digital currency in financial disclosure orders if there is evidence they have been used. She told the Financial Times: 'They can be used to run a parallel economy. People will go to immense lengths... as a spousal claim is more damaging than tax because it is half your wealth.' Bitcoin is a virtual currency that works without a central bank and can be sent over the internet. Courts in California are already issuing search and discovery orders for assets, including digital currencies like Bitcoin.

Det frygtes, at ægtefæller kan bruge Bitcoin til at skjule formue ved at overføre det mellem online wallets, til venner eller til områder uden for den juridiske jurisdiktion. Ayesha Vardag sagde, at flere skilsmisseadvokater kunne begynde at inkludere digital valuta i finansielle åbenhedspåbud, hvis der er bevis for, at det er blevet brugt. Hun fortalte Financial Times: 'De kan bruges til at drive en parallel økonomi. Folk vil gå meget langt... da et krav fra en ægtefælle er mere skadeligt end skat, fordi det er halvdelen af din formue.' Bitcoin er en virtuel valuta, der fungerer uden en centralbank og kan overføres over internettet. Retterne i Californien udsteder allerede kendelser om ransagning og opdagelse af aktiver, herunder digitale valutaer som Bitcoin.

article_content: By Kieran Corcoran. A pair of sharpened metal claws, believed to have been used in ritual combat, has been discovered by archaeologists in Peru. The artefact, thought to be from the ancient Moche civilisation, was found in a nobleman's tomb in northern Peru. Experts were excavating at the Huaca de la Luna site near Trujillo when they uncovered the claws along with a sceptre, earrings, and a mask. Historians believe the claws were part of a costume used in a Moche combat ritual and would have been attached to an animal skin outfit. Archaeologist Santiago Uceda commented, 'The sceptre signifies power; the earrings, status; and the ceramic piece is typical of an elite personage.' The artefacts are believed to be over 1,500 years old. The Moche civilisation, centred around Trujillo, pre-dates the Inca society and declined around 800 AD. Further research is expected to provide a more precise age of the objects in around six months. The Moche civilisation emerged around the time of Christ and flourished for about 800 years. They were known for their artistic and agricultural advancements and constructed huacas, or pyramids, where artefacts like the claws were found.

Eksperter gravede på Huaca de la Luna nær Trujillo og afdækkede kløerne sammen med en scepter, øreringe og en maske. Historikere mener, at kløerne var en del af en kostume brugt i en Moche kamp ritual og ville have været fastgjort til et dyreskindstøj. Arkæolog Santiago Uceda sagde, 'Sceptret symboliserer magt; øreringene, status; og den keramiske genstand er typisk for en elitepersonlighed.' Artefakterne menes at være over 1.500 år gamle. Moche civilisationen, centreret omkring Trujillo, er ældre end Inka civilisationen og forsvandt omkring 800 e.Kr. Yderligere forskning vil give en mere præcis alder for genstandene om seks måneder. De var kendt for deres kunstneriske og landbrugsmæssige fremskridt og byggede huacas, eller pyramider, hvor artefakter som kløerne blev fundet.

article_content: A remarkable collection of letters written by the future kings Edward VIII and George VI has surfaced, revealing their deep disappointment at being barred from fighting in World War I. The candid correspondence, addressed to Admiral Sir William Campbell Tait, their mentor during the war, showcases the princes' frustration and longing to be part of the action. Edward VIII, who was heir to the throne, was prohibited from active service by Secretary of State for War Lord Kitchener, while George VI was held back due to health issues, including gastric problems and an ulcer. The letters, written between 1912 and 1932 on Buckingham Palace letterhead, offer a unique glimpse into the personal lives and feelings of the royal family during a pivotal moment in history. In one letter, Edward expresses his envy of servicemen on the front line, stating, 'Oh god!! How I envy you all on active service, ready to deliver to those bloody Germans what I hope and am confident will be their death blow!!' George, on the other hand, writes about his relief at having an abscess removed from his navel and his efforts to stay entertained while recovering from illness. The collection, which includes a self-portrait by Edward and a Christmas card from George, has been meticulously restored by Admiral Tait's family and is set to be auctioned for an estimated £45,000. The letters not only highlight the princes' desire to serve but also touch on their personal struggles, such as George's stammer and Edward's experiences at Oxford University, where he was part of the exclusive Bullingdon Club.

Korrespondancen, som er adresseret til admiral Sir William Campbell Tait, deres mentor under krigen, viser prinsens frustration og længsel efter at være en del af indsatsen. Edward VIII, som var tronfølger, blev forhindret i aktiv tjeneste af krigsminister Lord Kitchener, mens George VI blev holdt tilbage på grund af helbredsproblemer, herunder maveproblemer og et mavesår. Brevene, som er skrevet mellem 1912 og 1932 på Buckingham Palace-papir, giver et unikt indblik i de kongelige familiemedlemmers personlige liv og følelser under en afgørende historisk begivenhed. I et brev udtrykker Edward sin misundelse over for frontlinjetjenestemændene og siger: 'Åh gud!! Sådan misunner jeg jer alle på aktiv tjeneste, klar til at give de blodige tyskere, hvad jeg håber og er overbevist om vil blive deres dødsslag!!' George skriver på den anden side om sin lettelse over at have fået fjernet en byld fra navlen og hans bestræbelser på at holde sig underholdt, mens han kommer sig fra sygdom. Samlingen, som omfatter et selvportræt af Edward og et julekort fra George, er blevet omhyggeligt restaureret af admiral Tait's familie og skal sælges på auktion for et estimeret beløb på £45.000. The documentary is replete with personal narratives of women who have chosen to embrace their natural hair and the opinions of men who frequent barbershops, providing a nuanced view of the issue. A striking scene in a bustling Houston barbershop encapsulates the prevailing attitude towards hair among some black men. Farris-Lewis sheds light on the pervasive 'social conditioning' that black people worldwide face when it comes to their hair. The film also captures the emotional testimony of an elderly man who laments the erosion of 'respect' for black people who opt for natural hairstyles. At its core, 'New Growth' is a tribute to those who have chosen to forgo chemical treatments and embrace their natural beauty. Farris-Lewis's personal story, marked by her daughter's hair loss due to a relaxer, serves as the impetus for her advocacy. She squarely places the blame on media, particularly Hollywood and music videos, for perpetuating damaging beauty standards that have far-reaching consequences. The documentary also provides a platform for women who choose to straighten their hair, highlighting the complex societal dynamics at play. Farris-Lewis is adamant that her film is not a critique but a celebration of those who have chosen to go natural. She is currently working on new projects and is keen to hear from African women about their experiences with hair and beauty standards.

article_content: ISLAMABAD - Afghan officials report a 'coordinated' suicide car bombing hit a 'high-profile' security forces' convoy in Kabul on Tuesday, resulting in at least 13 deaths and nine injuries.
